direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale captures the beauty and seclusion of Easter Island well and helps build the backdrop of the Chilean coup having an impact on the characters; the direction on a microscale feels very Martin McDonagh as it uses his signature two-protagonist structure to create interpersonal scenes that are both funny and profound; the storytelling is pretty straightforward as it uses a looming death to help raise the stakes as the movie goes on; they build emotional tension pretty well as you get a sense of attachment to these characters as the movie goes on, so you feel for them whenever something bad happens to them

performance.comments: The emotional core for the movie as he uses his aloof, but serious nature to really help provide personality to the character as you really get invested in his story throughout the movie as he reflects on his life; all the performances really flow through him as he has great chemistry with Sam Rockwell and good chemistry with the remaining cast

The story really feels like it is told from his perspective as he is the perfect partner to Malkovich in helping get the best out of not only his partner but himself as well; plays into the comedy very well and has good chemistry with the cast as he shows why he is one of the best working actors in Hollywood right now

Not in the movie for that long but makes his presence known as he is easily the funniest actor in the movie; he really lights up the room with his presence and shows how there are no small parts, just small actors
Plays her student character well as she shows the voice of youth during that time period; has good chemistry with Malkovich
Really isn't in the movie for that long, but has enjoyable scenes with Rockwell

cast.comments: The chemistry as a whole works very well as everyone is able to work well off each other to help move the movie forward and bring the best out of the comedic moments

story.comments: The concept is a fictional story set across a real conflict and uses the traditional Martin McDonagh dual-protagonist idea to show the impact the CIA has on the world and how it intervenes in other countries' politics; the plot structure is linear, but you understand the looming conflict and end so the tension throughout the movie builds until the climax you already expect (making it have much more emotional weight with the journey you go on with these characters); character writing is very good as they provide empathy and humor to both of the main leads, especially Malkovich, as you grow to love them until the very end (which makes the ending have much more emotional weight as you understand the dynamic the two characters have); additionally, the character writing for the supporting characters is also good as you do see the fight the students have while you get to laugh at characters like Steve Buscemi and Parker Posey

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very Martin McDonagh-esque as it infuses a lot of humor and profanity to keep you entertained as you see how the plot unfolds; the humor is very instrumental to the movie as it uses a lot of comedy and profanity; the symbolism is pretty strong as the movie deals a lot with grief, letting go, and American interference in global politics; the foreshadowing is good as you understand the looming ending for the movie when it starts, so it uses your emotional weight and connection to the characters to help get you to this eventual ending

score.comments: Helps set the tone and setting for the movie

soundtrack.comments: Helps set the time period and setting

cinematography.comments: Shot very well as it feels polished and shows the beauty and seclusion of Easter Island; the way the interpersonal scenes are shot feels very similar to other Martin McDonagh movies; the inclusion of Super 8 footage helps transport you back to the 1970s

editing.comments: Very sharp and polished, feeling typical of other Martin McDonagh movies

sound.comments: Executed well and helps give the movie a bit of a '70s feel

production_design.comments: Transports you to both 1970s Chile and Easter Island, capturing the beauty of the time period and the unique island setting

makeup.comments: Helps stylize the characters to make the movie feel like it's set in the '70s

costumes.comments: Helps stylize the characters to make the movie feel like it's set in the '70s

review.pacing: A bit on the slower side because the movie is very dialogue-heavy, but only really 5 to 10 minutes could have been cut because the film is still very enjoyable
review.climax: Executed very well because the climax is set up right from the beginning; knowing the looming ending from the start gives the climax tremendous emotional weight after the journey you go on with these characters
review.tone: Feels very much like a Martin McDonagh dark comedy with atmospheric period flavors that transport you to the 1970s
review.overall: Overall, 'Wild Horse Nine' is a funny, sharp, and emotionally resonant dark comedy that very much feels like a Martin McDonagh film, utilizing the beautiful seclusion of Easter Island and the backdrop of the 1973 Chilean coup to tell a poignant story about grief, mortality, and CIA interference; anchored by stellar lead chemistry between John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell alongside a hilarious turn from Steve Buscemi, showing the consistency Martin McDonagh has in delivering very good movies to this scale
